rationale:
Issue #12 ('ensureSupportsAnsi throws exception on Mac/VSCode') describes a runtime failure on macOS. The minimized production patch restructures checkAnsiSupport to add a non-Windows fallback path that returns true when attached to a valid stream OR the terminal type is bash, fixing the false-negative detection that caused the exception. The patch contains no formatting, refactor, documentation, or test-only changes—only the conditional logic fix. The trigger tests from later commit c8c4bdb mock terminal.runsOnWindows=false, terminal.supportsAnsi=false, terminal.attachedToValidStream=true/false, and processManager.determineTerminalType()=TerminalType.bash, then expect the new disjunctive condition to hold. These tests are semantically equivalent to the reported defect: they exercise the same non-Windows code path that previously returned false and now returns true when the terminal type is bash. The tests do not depend on any new production API introduced by the fix (determineTerminalType and TerminalType.bash already existed). Strict validation passed all checks: both versions build, 9 trigger tests reproduced deterministically on buggy (AB/BA/AB validation passed per strict_original and strict_post_minimization), all tests pass on fixed, and full-suite failures on buggy include only the 9 reproduced triggers. No duplicate root cause exists in active_same_project_root_causes.

Issue #12 ('ensureSupportsAnsi throws exception on Mac/VSCode', label 'bug', closed 2023-05-17T15:20:46Z) is linked to fix commit f840a62 via PR #31 with traceability path fix_commit_to_issue and verified_fix_issue_numbers=[12]. The minimized production patch is a single hunk in lib/src/controller.dart that restructures AnsiXController.checkAnsiSupport so the non-Windows branch gains a fallback (attachedToValidStream || determineTerminalType() == TerminalType.bash) instead of falling through to a false result; this is exactly the pre-existing behavior that made ensureSupportsAnsi throw on macOS/VSCode. The minimized patch contains only that behavioral change: no renames, no formatting-only edits, no new public API, no docs or config files (production_files lists one file; commit_stats reports 1 production hunk, 8 changed lines). The trigger comes from test/ansix/ansix_test.dart in the maintainer's own change set and only stubs determineTerminalType() and adjusts expectations on the existing non-Windows ('other') parametrized cases for checkAnsiSupport and ensureSupportsAnsi; determineTerminalType() and TerminalType.bash are not added anywhere in the fix diff and build.both_versions passed, so the trigger compiles and runs against the buggy revision without depending on a fix-introduced API. Strict evidence for both the original and post-minimization runs reports passed=true with no failed checks: 9 declared selectors present and unique, trigger.buggy_differential reproduced all 9, trigger.fixed_clean and full_suite.fixed_all_green green, full_suite.buggy_reproduces_only_triggers satisfied, determinism over 3 repetitions across an 80-run matrix. active_same_project_root_causes is empty and nikosportolos/ansix#12 is the only allowed root cause id, so no duplicate.
